speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you have been experiencing fever and altered mental status for the last two days; to begin my assessment, can you please describe exactly how your mental state has changed, such as confusion, lethargy, or hallucinations?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of fever and altered mentation, reporting fever without chills and rigors. He denies sore throat, abdominal pain, headache, loose stool, burning micturition, or seizures. Has a history of tics and is currently taking haloperidol.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. You mentioned a history of tics and taking haloperidol; are you currently experiencing any new or worsening muscle stiffness, tremors, or a "lead-pipe" sensation in your limbs? Also, have you noticed any changes in your bowel habits or urine output?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Fever and altered mentation. I also have Profuse sweating, Generalized rigidity, Confusion and disorientation, Ability to move all limbs, Normal deep tendon reflexes with bilateral downgoing plantar responses.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome (NMS)

The clinical picture of fever, altered mental status, generalized rigidity, and profuse sweating in a patient taking haloperidol is classic for NMS. Please REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count, Creatine Kinase, and Basic Metabolic Panel to confirm muscle breakdown and metabolic derangement.
